decision: Accept or reject the port of the OSS cell-list + neighbour-index storage scheme into TensorLBM as an alternative traversal for wall-bounded D2Q9 flows.

alternatives.A_dense_baseline: TensorLBM dense traversal (Q,L,H) arrays, pull gather + collide, halfway bounce-back by explicit wall masking (independent implementation).
alternatives.B_tl_sparse: TensorLBM list-based port: flag grid -> (cell list, (N,Q-1) uint32 index array), streaming by 1-D indirection, no-slip by index aliasing. Index array built by src/tensorlbm/sparse_list_aos.build_index_array.
alternatives.C_oss_index: Same traversal as B, but the index array is produced by the OSS function lbmpy.sparse.SparseLbMapper.create_index_array (executed in-process) and injected verbatim; populations reordered to the lbmpy LBStencil(D2Q9) ordering.

hypotheses.H1: The ported index array is bit-identical to the OSS index array on the same flag grid (integer equality, no tolerance).
hypotheses.H2: Sparse (B) and dense (A) arms produce the same populations to round-off for the same discrete scheme (they differ only in storage/traversal).
hypotheses.H3: Both arms reproduce the analytic references within the owner tolerance (15%); the expected level is <=1% for plane Poiseuille and <=2% for the Taylor-Green decay rate.
hypotheses.H4: Mixing the AoS stride convention (offset = cell*Q + d) with the OSS index array (offset = cell + d*N) silently corrupts the solution -- i.e. the OSS 'AoS' label refers to the (N,Q) list, while its addressing is SoA.

outcome_metrics.sparse_vs_dense: max|u_B - u_A| / u_max over fluid cells (steady state)
outcome_metrics.poiseuille_profile_error: Linf and L2 relative error of u_x(y) vs u = G/(2 nu) (y+1/2)(H - (y+1/2))
outcome_metrics.taylor_green_decay_error: |omega_measured - omega_analytic| / omega_analytic with omega = 2 nu k^2

T5_mass_conservation.metric: max |sum rho - N| / N over the run

stopping_rule: Steady state: max|u(t+200)-u(t)|/u_max < 1e-12, capped at 120000 steps. If the cap is hit the case is reported as not converged and the metric is marked WITHHELD.

changed: storage/traversal (dense vs list-based) and the code path that builds the index array (TensorLBM vs OSS)
nuisance: summation order (float round-off) - expected at the 1e-15 level, hence threshold 1e-12

repetitions: Deterministic: no random seeds in the reported runs (the only stochastic input is a fixed-seed perturbation used in the one-step equivalence unit test). One run per configuration; the grid sweep (H=8,16,32,64) and the tau sweep provide the replication axis.
environment: local compute node (x86_64, 128 cores), python 3.11, numpy 2.4.6, lbmpy 2.0, pystencils 2.0; float64 throughout; BLAS not used.
analysis: Report per-case tables with ref/got/error/pass; convergence as the observed order p = log2(e_H/e_2H); sensitivity to tau and to the number of active cells; no post-hoc threshold tuning.
safety_and_resources: Runtime < 5 min single core, memory < 100 MB, no cluster submission needed (well under the 10 min cluster rule).
